questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: Which writ is issued by a court to command a public authority to perform a public duty it has failed or refused to perform?
explanations: Habeas corpus protects against unlawful detention.
Correct. Mandamus commands a public authority to perform a public or statutory duty.
Prohibition restrains a lower court or tribunal from exceeding jurisdiction.
Certiorari is used to quash an order of a lower court or tribunal in appropriate cases.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; Fundamental Rights; constitutional remedies.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.subtopic: Public finance; revenue and capital expenditure
questions.stem: Which of the following is generally classified as capital expenditure by a government?
options: Construction of a new public hospital building
explanations: Salaries are normally revenue expenditure because they do not create a durable asset.
Interest payments are revenue expenditure.
Correct. Construction of a public hospital creates a durable public asset and is classified as capital expenditure.
Routine subsidies are generally revenue expenditure.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana; public finance and government expenditure.

questions.stem: A directed weighted graph contains a reachable negative-weight cycle. Which statement about single-source shortest paths is correct?
options: Dijkstra always finds finite shortest paths
Bellman-Ford can detect the negative-weight cycle
A topological ordering always removes the cycle
Breadth-first search gives correct weighted shortest paths
explanations: Dijkstra's algorithm does not correctly handle arbitrary negative edge weights or reachable negative cycles.
Correct. Bellman-Ford relaxes edges repeatedly and can detect a further relaxation after |V|−1 passes, indicating a reachable negative-weight cycle.
A directed graph with a cycle is not a DAG and has no topological ordering.
BFS minimises edge count in unweighted graphs, not arbitrary weighted path cost.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; graph algorithms and shortest paths.

questions.stem: In a CRC system, the dataword is 1101 and the generator is 1011. Which operation is used to obtain the transmitted codeword?
options: Append three zeros, perform modulo-2 division by 1011, and append the remainder to the dataword
Divide 1011 by 1101 using ordinary integer division
Append the generator itself to the dataword
explanations: Correct. The generator degree is 3, so append three zeros, perform modulo-2 polynomial division, then append the 3-bit remainder to the original dataword.
CRC uses modulo-2 division (XOR arithmetic), not ordinary integer addition.
The data polynomial is divided by the generator after appending zero bits; this reverses the roles.
The generator is not appended as the CRC remainder.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; error detection and CRC.

questions.stem: A process references pages 1, 2, 3, 1, 4 with three initially empty frames. Under FIFO replacement, how many page faults occur?
explanations: Three is incorrect because page 4 causes a fault after the three frames are filled.
Correct. References 1, 2 and 3 fault; the second reference to 1 hits; page 4 faults, giving four faults.
Five would incorrectly count the repeated reference to page 1 as a fault.
Two ignores the initial page loads.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; Virtual memory; page replacement.

questions.stem: In SQL, what does COUNT(column_name) return when some rows contain NULL in that column?
options: The total number of rows including NULLs
The number of non-NULL values in that column
The number of distinct non-NULL values only
Always zero if any NULL exists
explanations: COUNT(*) counts rows, including rows with NULLs.
Correct. COUNT(column_name) counts non-NULL values in that column.
COUNT(DISTINCT column_name) counts distinct non-NULL values.
The presence of NULL values does not force the count to zero.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; SQL; aggregate functions and NULL.

questions.stem: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time and is stable in its standard array implementation?
explanations: Heap sort has O(n log n) worst-case time but is not stable in its standard in-place form.
Correct. Merge sort has O(n log n) worst-case time and is stable when equal keys are merged consistently.
Selection sort has O(n²) time in the usual implementation.
Quicksort has O(n²) worst-case time and is not stable in its standard form.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; Sorting; asymptotic complexity.

questions.stem: In DFA minimisation, two states are equivalent if:
options: They have the same state names
No input string distinguishes their acceptance behaviour
They have identical outgoing transition labels only
explanations: State names have no bearing on equivalence.
Correct. States are equivalent when every possible suffix leads to the same acceptance result from both states.
Matching labels alone is insufficient; destination behaviour matters.
Two accepting states may still be distinguishable by some input string.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; Finite automata; distinguishability and minimisation.

questions.subtopic: Memory hierarchy; average memory access time
questions.stem: A cache has hit time 2 ns, miss penalty 50 ns and hit ratio 0.9. Using AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty, what is AMAT?
explanations: 5 ns would require a miss penalty contribution of 3 ns, not 5.
Correct. AMAT=2+(0.1×50)=7 ns.
10 ns overstates the miss contribution.
52 ns ignores the high hit ratio.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; Memory hierarchy; average memory access time.

questions.stem: Events A and B are independent, with P(A)=0.4 and P(B)=0.5. What is P(A∩B)?
explanations: 0.1 is not the product of the independent event probabilities.
Correct. Independence gives P(A∩B)=0.4×0.5=0.2.
0.4 is P(A), not the intersection probability.
0.9 is the sum, not the intersection.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; Conditional probability; independence.

questions.stem: For the expression a-b-c, if subtraction is left-associative, it is parsed as:
explanations: This is right-associative grouping.
Correct. Left associativity groups the leftmost operation first: (a-b)-c.
The expression is valid under ordinary arithmetic grammar.
The second operation is subtraction, not addition.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; Parsing; operator precedence and associativity.

questions.stem: In a singly linked list with only a head pointer, inserting a node at the beginning takes:
explanations: Correct. Set the new node's next pointer to the old head and update head; this is constant time.
No traversal or logarithmic search is required.
Linear time is needed for traversal-based operations, not insertion at the head.
There is no sorting or divide-and-conquer operation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; Linked lists; pointer operations.

questions.stem: A network is divided using a /26 prefix. How many usable host addresses are available in each ordinary IPv4 subnet, assuming network and broadcast addresses are reserved?
explanations: 30 usable hosts corresponds to a /27 subnet.
Correct. A /26 leaves 6 host bits: 2⁶=64 total addresses, minus network and broadcast gives 62 usable hosts.
64 is the total address count, not the usable host count.
126 usable hosts corresponds to a /25 subnet.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; IPv4; subnetting and address allocation.

questions.stem: A schedule is conflict-serializable if and only if its precedence graph is:
explanations: Completeness is not the serializability criterion.
Correct. A schedule is conflict-serializable exactly when its precedence (serialization) graph has no directed cycle.
Strong connectivity is not required and would not be the criterion.
Bipartiteness is unrelated to conflict serializability.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; Concurrency control; serializability.

questions.stem: For matrix-chain multiplication, the dynamic-programming method primarily minimises:
options: The memory addresses used by matrices
explanations: The number of matrices in the chain is fixed by the input.
Correct. Matrix-chain order optimisation chooses parenthesisation to minimise scalar multiplication cost.
The chain produces one final product matrix.
Memory addresses are not the objective of the standard matrix-chain cost recurrence.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; Dynamic programming; matrix-chain multiplication.

questions.stem: A binary semaphore initially set to 1 is used as a mutex. What happens when a process successfully performs wait(P) on it?
options: Its value becomes 0 and the process enters the critical section if the lock was free
All waiting processes enter the critical section together
explanations: Correct. wait decrements the available permit from 1 to 0, granting exclusive entry; another process must wait until signal(V).
A binary semaphore does not increase to 2 in this use.
Mutual exclusion permits only one process in the critical section at a time.
The semaphore remains a synchronisation object and can be signalled.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; Process synchronisation; semaphores.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: A joint sitting of Parliament to resolve a deadlock on an ordinary bill is presided over by:

The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
explanations: The President summons a joint sitting but does not preside over it.
The Vice-President chairs the Rajya Sabha, not a joint sitting.

The Deputy Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha in the Chairman's absence, not ordinarily over a joint sitting.

Borrowing costs tend to rise, moderating credit demand

A repo-rate change does not mechanically double the money supply.
Tax revenue does not automatically increase as an immediate mechanical result.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology

The electrical resistance of the coil only
explanations: A constant flux does not induce emf merely by being present; change in flux matters.
Correct. Induced emf magnitude is proportional to the time rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.
Resistance affects current for a given emf, not the induced emf law itself.
The law does not state a square-current relationship.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: Which statement about the enhanced greenhouse effect is scientifically correct?
options: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit outgoing longwave radiation, increasing heat retention
The ozone hole is the sole cause of global warming
Greenhouse gases prevent all incoming solar radiation
The greenhouse effect occurs only in urban areas
explanations: Correct. Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit portions of outgoing terrestrial longwave radiation, changing Earth's energy balance.
Ozone depletion and global warming are distinct phenomena; the ozone hole is not the sole cause.
Most incoming shortwave solar radiation still reaches Earth's surface.
The natural greenhouse effect operates globally, not only in cities.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies; Climate change; greenhouse effect.

68 overstates the combined average.

UNESCO works in education, science and culture.

questions.stem: A five-stage pipeline has a 2 ns clock period and no stalls. In steady state, what is its ideal instruction throughput?

Dividing the clock period by the number of stages is incorrect.

questions.stem: In a conventional compiler, which phase groups character sequences into tokens such as identifiers, keywords and numeric literals?
explanations: Syntax analysis consumes tokens and checks grammatical structure.

Semantic analysis checks meaning-related constraints such as types and declarations.
Intermediate-code generation occurs after earlier analysis phases.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; lexical analysis.

questions.stem: A transaction transfers ₹500 from account A to account B. Which ACID property ensures that the debit and credit occur as one indivisible unit?
explanations: Consistency ensures that constraints and valid database states are preserved.
Isolation concerns interference between concurrent transactions.
Correct. Atomicity means either all operations of the transfer occur or none do.
Durability ensures committed changes survive failures.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; transactions and concurrency control.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.subtopic: Constitutional bodies; Comptroller and Auditor General

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana

questions.stem: Nominal GDP rises by 8% while the GDP deflator rises by 5%. Approximately how much does real GDP rise?
explanations: Adding nominal growth and inflation overstates real growth.

questions.stem: A random variable X takes values 0, 1 and 2 with probabilities 1/4, 1/2 and 1/4 respectively. What is Var(X)?
explanations: Incorrect. This is not the second central moment.
Correct. E(X)=1 and E(X²)=3/2, so Var(X)=3/2−1=1/2.
Incorrect. This is not E(X²)−[E(X)]².
Incorrect. The variance is 1/2, not 1.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; expectation and variance.

questions.stem: A 3×4 matrix has rank 3. The dimension of its null space is:
explanations: Incorrect. A 3×4 matrix with rank 3 has one free variable.
Correct. By rank–nullity, nullity = number of columns − rank = 4−3=1.
Incorrect. This would require rank 2.
Incorrect. This would require rank 1.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Linear Algebra; rank and nullity.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: A connected undirected graph has 10 vertices and 9 edges. Which statement must be true?
explanations: Incorrect. A connected graph with V−1 edges has no cycle.
Correct. A connected graph with V−1 edges is a tree.
Incorrect. A tree need not have every vertex of degree 2.
Incorrect. A complete graph on 10 vertices has 45 edges.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Graph Theory; trees.

questions.stem: A direct-mapped cache has 64 lines. Main-memory block number 205 maps to which cache line, using zero-based indexing?
explanations: Incorrect. 205 mod 64 = 13, not 11.
Correct. Direct mapping uses block number mod number of lines: 205 mod 64 = 13.
Incorrect. 17 is not the remainder of 205 divided by 64.
Incorrect. The remainder is 13, not 21.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; cache mapping.

questions.stem: If T(n)=2T(n/2)+n log n, with T(1)=Θ(1), what is the asymptotic solution?
explanations: Incorrect. This omits the additional logarithmic factor from the recurrence.
Correct. At each of log n levels, the non-recursive work totals Θ(n log(n/2^i)); summing gives Θ(n log² n).
Incorrect. The recurrence does not produce quadratic growth.
Incorrect. The recursion processes Θ(n) total input work per level.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; recurrence relations and asymptotic analysis.

questions.stem: Which operation is guaranteed to preserve regularity when applied to two regular languages L1 and L2?
explanations: Correct. Regular languages are closed under intersection, using product construction of finite automata.
Incorrect. Regular languages have several closure properties, including intersection.
Incorrect. Concatenation is also closed for regular languages.
Incorrect. Complement is closed by swapping accepting and non-accepting states in a complete DFA.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; closure properties of regular languages.

questions.stem: A schedule has precedence-graph edges T1→T2, T2→T3 and T1→T3, with no other edges. The schedule is:
options: Not conflict serializable because it has three edges.
Conflict serializable in the order T1, T2, T3.
Conflict serializable in the order T3, T2, T1.
Not conflict serializable because every transaction must have an incoming edge.
explanations: Incorrect. The number of edges does not determine serializability; cycles do.

Incorrect. This order violates the directed edges.
Incorrect. A source transaction may have no incoming edge.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; conflict serializability.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy

questions.stem: Find the next term: 3, 8, 18, 38, 78, __.
explanations: Incorrect. The sequence does not follow this increment.

questions.stem: In TCP Reno, when three duplicate ACKs are received, the sender typically:

Retransmits the missing segment and enters fast recovery
explanations: Incorrect. That describes the response to a retransmission timeout in simplified Reno behavior.

questions.stem: For F(A,B,C)=Σm(1,3,5,7), the minimized expression is:
explanations: A is not common to all minterms.
B is not common to all minterms.
All listed minterms have C=1; hence F=C.
A+B is zero for minterm 1.

questions.stem: A load is immediately followed by an instruction using its destination register. Without forwarding or scheduling, this is a:
explanations: Structural hazards arise from resource conflicts.

Control hazards arise from branches.
A page fault is a memory-management event.

questions.stem: Which structure is most directly used to evaluate a postfix expression?
explanations: A queue is FIFO, not LIFO.

A search tree is unnecessary.
An adjacency list represents graph edges.

questions.stem: A predictive LL(1) parser requires its parsing-table entries to be:

explanations: An empty table cannot parse input.

LL(1) parsing avoids backtracking.
Left recursion must be eliminated for ordinary LL(1) parsing.

questions.stem: A system is safe if:
options: A safe sequence exists in which every process can finish
explanations: A safe state can contain active processes.
Correct: a safe sequence demonstrates completion without deadlock.
Processes may hold resources in a safe state.
All resources being free is sufficient but not necessary.

questions.stem: 100% statement coverage guarantees that:
options: Every executable statement ran at least once
explanations: Statement coverage does not imply path coverage.
Branch coverage is a separate, stronger metric.
Correct: every executable statement has been executed.
Coverage cannot prove absence of defects.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Modern India with special emphasis on Indian National Movement
questions.stem: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in:
explanations: 1919 saw the Rowlatt Satyagraha and Jallianwala Bagh events.

explanations: Correct: the past perfect shows the repair was completed before the later past event (the team's arrival).
The present perfect does not fit the completed past-time sequence introduced by 'By the time ... arrived'.
The simple present does not express the earlier completed action in this past narrative.
The future tense is inconsistent with the past reference point.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: English.

questions.stem: Choose the best replacement for the underlined idea: 'The committee discussed about the proposal.'
options: had discussion about on the proposal
explanations: 'Discuss' is transitive and normally takes a direct object.
Correct: 'Discussed the proposal' is idiomatic and grammatical.
The prepositions are redundant and incorrect.
The phrase uses unnecessary and incorrect prepositions.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: English.

questions.stem: The principal purpose of the United Nations Security Council's permanent-member veto is to:
options: Allow any member state to veto General Assembly elections
Require concurrence of the permanent members on substantive decisions, subject to the Charter's rules
Give permanent members control over the International Court of Justice's judgments
Permit unilateral amendment of the UN Charter
explanations: The veto is not a general power over General Assembly elections.
Correct: A negative vote by a permanent member can block substantive decisions under the Charter framework.
The ICJ is independent; the veto does not control its judgments.
Charter amendments require the prescribed ratification process.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.stem: A district's irrigation coverage rises, but agricultural output does not. Which additional evidence is most useful before concluding that irrigation investment failed?
options: Only the number of inauguration ceremonies
Cropping pattern, water reliability, soil quality, input use and weather variation
The number of kilometres of roads built
explanations: Ceremonies do not measure functional irrigation or productivity.
Correct: These variables help distinguish infrastructure failure from agronomic, climatic or utilisation constraints.
Population density alone cannot explain the production response.
Road length is not the key causal evidence in this question.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Telangana Economy.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state
questions.stem: The Telangana armed struggle of the late 1940s was directed primarily against:
options: The Nizam-era feudal order and oppressive landlordism, especially in affected rural areas
The introduction of the Indian Constitution in 1950
The establishment of the Planning Commission
explanations: Correct: The struggle challenged feudal exploitation and the Nizam-era political order.
The struggle predates the Constitution's commencement.
The 1956 reorganisation occurred later.
The Planning Commission was not the target of the armed struggle.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Telangana History.

questions.topic: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy
questions.stem: A State Legislature passes a law on a Concurrent List subject that conflicts with an earlier Parliamentary law. In the ordinary case, which rule applies?
options: The State law always prevails within the State.
The Parliamentary law prevails to the extent of repugnancy, unless the State law has received Presidential assent under Article 254(2), subject to Parliament's later overriding power.
The State law is automatically void in its entirety.
The Governor alone decides which law prevails.
explanations: State law does not automatically prevail.
Correct: Article 254(1) sets the general rule; Article 254(2) provides a qualified exception, and Parliament may later override.
Repugnancy generally affects the conflicting extent, not necessarily the entire statute.
This is a constitutional rule, not a unilateral gubernatorial choice.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Polity.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: Which gas is the largest contributor to anthropogenic radiative forcing among the long-lived greenhouse gases discussed in basic climate science?
explanations: Correct: CO₂ is the largest contributor among these long-lived anthropogenic greenhouse gases.
Argon is not a significant greenhouse gas.
Neon is not a significant greenhouse gas.
Hydrogen is not conventionally counted as a direct long-lived greenhouse gas in this comparison.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Environment.

questions.topic: Environmental issues; Disaster Management – Prevention and Mitigation Strategies
questions.stem: In a flood early-warning system, which combination is most appropriate?
options: Hazard monitoring, forecast thresholds, communication protocol and pre-identified response actions
Only a siren installed at the district headquarters
explanations: Correct: An effective warning chain links monitoring to actionable communication and response.
Maps support preparedness but do not provide a complete warning system.
A single siren may not reach exposed communities or communicate actions.
Damage assessment is retrospective.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Disaster Management.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.stem: Which institution is primarily responsible for monetary policy formulation in India under the current statutory framework?
options: Reserve Bank of India through the Monetary Policy Committee
explanations: NITI Aayog is a policy think tank, not the monetary authority.
Correct: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee determines the policy rate framework under the RBI Act.
The Finance Commission recommends tax devolution and grants.
The CAG audits public accounts.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Economy.

questions.topic: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation
questions.stem: Five pumps A, B, C, D and E are tested in a row. A must be before C; D must be immediately after B; E cannot be first. Which arrangement is valid?
explanations: Correct: A precedes C, D immediately follows B, and E is not first.
D is not immediately after B.
E is first, violating the condition.
D is not immediately after B.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Reasoning.

questions.topic: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation
questions.stem: A pipeline loses 12% of the water entering it. If 440 kilolitres reach consumers, how much water entered the pipeline?
explanations: Correct: 88% of input = 440, so input = 440/0.88 = 500 kL.
512 does not satisfy the 88% relation.
528 is 120% of 440, not the required input.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Data Interpretation.

questions.topic: Physical, Social and Economic Geography and Demography of Telangana
questions.stem: For identifying a watershed boundary in a hilly region, which field feature is most reliable?
options: A line joining the lowest points of valleys
A ridge or divide separating directions of surface runoff
explanations: Valley bottoms commonly collect runoff rather than divide it.
Correct: A watershed divide follows topographic highs separating drainage directions.
Administrative boundaries need not follow drainage divides.
Road alignments are not a hydrological boundary criterion.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Telangana Geography.

questions.topic: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Modern India with special emphasis on Indian National Movement
questions.stem: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed, among other things:
options: Immediate partition into two fully sovereign States as its central proposal
A Union of India with a limited set of central subjects and groupings of provinces
A unitary constitution with all powers vested in the Governor-General
A return to the 1909 separate-electorate framework as the sole objective
explanations: Partition was not the Plan's central formal proposal, although partition later occurred.
Correct: It envisaged a Union handling specified subjects, with provincial groupings and substantial provincial autonomy.
It did not propose a fully unitary arrangement.
It was a constitutional transfer-of-power plan, not solely an electoral reform proposal.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Modern Indian History.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.stem: A water sample has pH 5. Which statement is correct compared with a sample of pH 6?
options: It has one-tenth the hydrogen-ion activity.
It has ten times the hydrogen-ion activity.
It has twice the hydrogen-ion activity.
It has one-hundredth the hydrogen-ion activity.
explanations: A one-unit lower pH means tenfold higher hydrogen-ion activity, not one-tenth.
Correct: pH is logarithmic; pH 5 has 10 times the hydrogen-ion activity of pH 6.
A factor of two is not the pH scale relationship.
A factor of 100 corresponds to a two-unit pH difference.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Science.

questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.stem: Which measure best captures multidimensional poverty rather than income poverty alone?
options: A composite of deprivations in health, education and living standards
Only the market value of household assets
explanations: Consumption is a monetary poverty measure, not a multidimensional index by itself.
Correct: Multidimensional poverty combines several non-income deprivation indicators.
Unemployment is one labour-market indicator, not a multidimensional poverty measure.
Assets alone omit health and education dimensions. Paper II — Computer Science and Information Technology (60)
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Development.

questions.stem: A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
explanations: There are 3 favourable ordered outcomes, not 6.
Correct: Six ordered pairs sum to 7 out of 36 equally likely outcomes.
Five is the wrong favourable count.
Seven is the sum, not the number of favourable outcomes.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics.

questions.stem: A random variable X has mean 10 and variance 9. For Y = 3X − 4, the variance of Y is:
explanations: Variance is not transformed by adding 3 or subtracting 4.
Multiplying by 3 multiplies variance by 9, not 3.
Correct: Var(3X−4)=3²Var(X)=9×9=81.
77 incorrectly subtracts the constant from the variance.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics.

questions.stem: A test has sensitivity 0.90, specificity 0.95, and disease prevalence 0.02. Approximately what is P(disease | positive)?
explanations: This is approximately prevalence × sensitivity, not the posterior probability.
Sensitivity is P(positive|disease), not P(disease|positive).
Specificity is P(negative|no disease), not the requested posterior.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics.

questions.stem: For a square matrix A, which condition guarantees that A is invertible?
options: Rank(A) is less than its order
explanations: A zero determinant implies singularity.
Rank deficiency implies singularity.
Correct: Non-zero determinant is equivalent to invertibility for a square matrix.
A zero eigenvalue implies determinant zero and hence non-invertibility.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Linear Algebra.

questions.stem: The eigenvalues of a 3×3 matrix A are 2, −1 and 4. What is det(A²)?
explanations: 5 is the trace of A, not det(A²).
det(A) is −8, but squaring A squares the determinant.
Correct: det(A²)=[det(A)]²=(2×−1×4)²=64.
49 has no relation to the product of squared eigenvalues.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Linear Algebra.

questions.stem: A relation R on integers is defined by aRb iff a−b is divisible by 5. Which property set is correct?
explanations: Correct: Congruence modulo 5 is an equivalence relation.
It is not antisymmetric on all integers: 1R6 and 6R1 but 1≠6.
Divisibility congruence is transitive.
Every integer differs from itself by zero, and divisibility by 5 is symmetric.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory and Algebra.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: A simple undirected graph has 10 vertices, each of degree 3. How many edges does it have?
explanations: The degree sum is 30, so the edge count is half of that.
Correct: By the handshaking lemma, 2E=10×3=30, hence E=15.
20 would imply degree sum 40.
30 is the degree sum, not the edge count.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Discrete Mathematics.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: A connected graph with n vertices and n−1 edges is necessarily:
options: A bipartite graph with equal partitions
explanations: Correct: A connected graph with exactly n−1 edges is acyclic and therefore a tree.
A complete graph generally has n(n−1)/2 edges.
A cycle has n edges and is not a tree.
Bipartiteness and equal partition sizes do not follow.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Graph Theory.

questions.stem: Which Boolean identity is equivalent to A + A'B?
explanations: A + A'B simplifies to A+B, not A'B.
Correct: Using absorption/distributive law, A + A'B = (A+A')(A+B)=A+B.
AB is not equivalent for A=1,B=0.
A'+B differs, for example at A=1,B=0.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic.

questions.stem: A 4-variable Karnaugh map contains 1s at minterms 0, 2, 8 and 10. Using variables A,B,C,D with A as MSB, the simplified function is:
explanations: Correct: The four minterms have B=0 and D=0 while A and C vary, giving B'D'.
B'D would require D=1.
BD' requires B=1.
A'C' would require A=0 and C=0, which does not cover all four minterms.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic.

questions.stem: A byte-addressable memory has 20 address lines. What is its maximum addressable capacity?
explanations: Twenty address lines do not mean 20 bytes.
Correct: 20 independent address bits select 2²⁰ byte locations.
This is not the address-space formula.
2¹⁰ locations would require only 10 address lines.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization.

questions.stem: A 5-stage pipeline has stage latencies 2, 3, 4, 2 and 3 ns. Ignoring register overhead, what is the ideal clock period?
explanations: The clock must accommodate the slowest stage, not the fastest.
3 ns is below the maximum stage latency.
Correct: The pipeline clock period is set by the maximum stage latency, 4 ns.
14 ns is the sum of stage latencies, approximating non-pipelined latency.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization.

questions.stem: In C, what is the value of sizeof(char) guaranteed to be?
explanations: A C byte is not necessarily one bit.
Correct: sizeof(char) is always 1; a byte is the size of a char in the C implementation.
It is not guaranteed to be 2 bytes.
The size is never zero.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: C Programming.

questions.stem: Consider: int a[]={10,20,30,40}; int *p=a; What is the value of *(p+2) - *(p+1)?
explanations: Correct: *(p+2)=30 and *(p+1)=20; the difference is 10.
20 is the second array element, not the arithmetic result.
30 is the third array element.
Both pointer expressions remain within the array; behaviour is defined.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: C Programming.

questions.stem: A queue is implemented using a circular array of size N with one slot deliberately left empty to distinguish full from empty. The maximum number of stored elements is:
explanations: One slot is reserved, so all N slots cannot hold data simultaneously.
Correct: Maximum occupancy is N−1.
N+1 exceeds the physical capacity.
Half the array is not the stated constraint.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Structures.

questions.stem: A binary min-heap contains n distinct keys. The worst-case time to find the maximum key is:
explanations: The root is the minimum, not the maximum.
The maximum is not necessarily on a single root-to-leaf path.
Correct: The maximum must be among the leaves; scanning them takes linear time.
Sorting the heap is unnecessary.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Structures.

questions.stem: For an array of n elements, binary search in the worst case requires:
explanations: A constant number is not sufficient for arbitrary n.
Correct: The search interval is approximately halved at each step.
Linear search has O(n) worst-case time.
O(n log n) is larger than necessary.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms.

questions.stem: An algorithm satisfies T(n)=2T(n/2)+n log n. By the Master Theorem, its asymptotic running time is:
explanations: The additive term is larger than n.
The regularity boundary case adds an additional logarithmic factor.
Correct: a=b=2, n^(log_b a)=n and f(n)=n log n, giving Θ(n log² n).
The recurrence does not yield quadratic growth.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms.

questions.stem: Which language is regular?
options: All binary strings containing an even number of 1s
explanations: Matching arbitrary counts of a and b is not regular.
The duplication language is not regular over the stated alphabet.
Correct: A DFA can track the parity of the number of 1s using two states.
Equal counts of three ordered symbol blocks are not regular.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation.

questions.stem: For a DFA with n states, the maximum number of states in the minimal DFA for its complement language is:
explanations: Complementing a complete DFA changes accepting states, not the state count.
Correct: The same complete transition graph recognises the complement by swapping final and non-final states.
2ⁿ is associated with subset construction from an NFA.
n! is not the bound for complementing a DFA.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation.

questions.stem: In a typical compiler, which phase is responsible for checking whether an identifier has been declared in the appropriate scope?
explanations: Lexical analysis recognises tokens.
Syntax analysis checks grammatical structure.
Correct: Declaration and scope checks are semantic-analysis tasks, typically using symbol-table information.
Code generation occurs after semantic checks.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design.

questions.stem: For the grammar E → E+T | T and T → T*F | F, which operator has higher precedence?
options: Precedence cannot be inferred from this grammar
explanations: The grammar places addition at the E level above T.
Correct: Multiplication is grouped within T, so it binds more tightly than addition.
The grammar explicitly separates the precedence levels.
The precedence is encoded by the grammar structure.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design.

questions.stem: Which scheduling algorithm can cause starvation of long processes when short jobs continually arrive?
explanations: FCFS does not normally starve a process already in the ready queue.
Correct: SJF may indefinitely postpone a long job if shorter jobs keep arriving.
Round Robin gives each ready process a time slice.
FIFO page replacement is not a CPU scheduling algorithm.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems.

questions.stem: A system uses 4 KiB pages and a 32-bit virtual address. Assuming a single-level page table and byte addressing, how many virtual pages exist?
explanations: 2¹⁰ is the number of pages only for a 22-bit page-number field.
2¹² is the page size in bytes, not the page count.
Correct: 4 KiB=2¹² bytes; page number bits=32−12=20, so 2²⁰ pages.
2³² is the number of byte addresses, not pages.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems.

questions.stem: A process holds resource R1 and requests R2. Another process holds R2 and requests R1. Both resources are non- preemptible and single-instance. Which deadlock condition is directly demonstrated?
explanations: Mutual exclusion is present, but the described cycle is more specifically circular wait.
Correct: P1 waits for R2 held by P2, while P2 waits for R1 held by P1, forming a cycle.
No preemption is also a condition, but it does not name the cycle shown.
Hold and wait is present, but the key relational structure is circular wait.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems.

questions.stem: In relational algebra, which operation removes duplicate tuples from a relation?
explanations: Correct: Classical relational projection returns a set of tuples and eliminates duplicates.
Selection filters rows but does not remove duplicates by itself.
Cartesian product combines tuples from two relations.
Rename changes relation or attribute names.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: DBMS.

questions.stem: A relation R(A,B,C) has functional dependencies A→B and B→C. Which statement is necessarily true?
options: A and B are candidate keys
explanations: Correct: By transitivity, A→B and B→C imply A→C.
The dependencies do not imply C→A.
No dependency establishes B→A.
A determines B and C, but B need not determine A; candidate-key status also depends on attributes and closure.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: DBMS.

questions.stem: Which SQL clause filters groups after aggregate functions have been computed?
explanations: WHERE filters rows before grouping/aggregation.
Correct: HAVING applies conditions to groups, commonly using aggregate expressions.
ORDER BY sorts the result.
DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: DBMS.

questions.stem: A transaction reads an item written by another transaction that later aborts. This is an example of:
explanations: Correct: Reading uncommitted data that is later rolled back is a dirty read.
A phantom involves a changing set of rows matching a predicate.
Lost update occurs when one write overwrites another without proper control.
A non-repeatable read is a repeated read returning a different committed value.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: DBMS.

questions.stem: A requirement states, 'The system shall respond to 95% of search requests within two seconds under 500 concurrent users.' This is primarily a:
explanations: It does not specify a business function.
Correct: It specifies measurable response-time and load characteristics.
A data-flow diagram is a modelling artefact.
A coding convention governs source-code style.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Software Engineering.

questions.stem: A team discovers that changing one module repeatedly breaks distant modules because of hidden dependencies. Which design property should be improved first?
options: Cohesion only by merging all modules
Loose coupling through explicit interfaces and dependency control
Code duplication to isolate each module
explanations: Merging all modules can worsen dependency problems; cohesion is not improved by indiscriminate merging.
Correct: Hidden cross-module dependencies indicate excessive coupling; explicit interfaces reduce it.
Adding branches can increase complexity and does not address dependencies.
Duplication may sometimes isolate dependencies but is not the general first design remedy.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Software Engineering.

questions.stem: Which OSI layer is responsible for end-to-end transport services such as reliable byte-stream delivery?
explanations: Network layer provides routing between networks.
Correct: The transport layer provides end-to-end process communication and may provide reliability.
Data Link handles node-to-node frame delivery.
Physical transmits raw bits over a medium.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks.

questions.stem: A /27 IPv4 subnet contains how many usable host addresses under conventional subnetting?
explanations: 16 is not the /27 usable-host count.
Correct: 32 total addresses minus network and broadcast = 30 usable hosts.
32 is the total address count, including network and broadcast.
62 is the usable count for a /26 subnet.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks.

questions.stem: A router receives an IPv4 packet whose TTL is 1. What should it do?
options: Forward it and set TTL to 0
Discard it and normally send ICMP Time Exceeded, subject to ICMP rules
explanations: A router must not forward a packet after TTL expiration.
Correct: Decrementing TTL would expire it; the router discards it and normally reports ICMP Time Exceeded.
Routers never increase TTL to extend packet life.
TTL expiration is unrelated to fragmentation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks.

questions.stem: In HTTP, which method is defined as safe and idempotent?
explanations: POST is not defined as safe or idempotent.
Correct: GET is safe and idempotent by HTTP semantics.
PATCH is not generally guaranteed to be idempotent.
CONNECT establishes a tunnel and is not the relevant safe retrieval method.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies.

questions.stem: A browser sends a cross-origin request with a non-simple method and custom header. Which mechanism is commonly used before the actual request?
options: CORS preflight using an OPTIONS request
explanations: DNS zone transfer is unrelated to browser cross-origin policy.
Correct: The browser commonly sends an OPTIONS preflight to ask whether the origin, method and headers are permitted.
TCP FIN closes a connection.
304 is a cache-validation response, not a CORS preflight.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies.

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: In Java, a method declared final:
options: Cannot be overridden in a subclass
explanations: A final method is implemented, not abstract.
Correct: A subclass cannot override a final method.
Overloading with a different parameter list may still be possible.
A final method need not be static.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOP and Java.

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: In C++, a base class intended for deletion through a base-class pointer when the dynamic object may be derived should generally have:
explanations: Deleting through a base pointer without a suitable virtual destructor can cause undefined behaviour.
Correct: A public virtual destructor enables correct derived-object destruction through a base pointer.
Destructors cannot be static.
An implicit destructor is not virtual merely because the class is a base class.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOP and C++.

questions.stem: A directed acyclic graph has vertices with indegrees (0,1,1,2). How many sources does it have?
explanations: A finite DAG must have at least one source.
Correct: Exactly one vertex has indegree zero.
There are not two zero-indegree vertices.
Four sources would require all four indegrees to be zero.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms.

questions.stem: Which data structure is most appropriate for evaluating a postfix expression in one left-to-right scan?
explanations: A queue does not provide last-in, first-out operand retrieval.
Correct: Push operands; on an operator, pop operands, evaluate, and push the result.
A search tree is unnecessary for operand evaluation.
A hash table does not model the required evaluation order.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Structures.

questions.stem: A 3-to-8 decoder has how many output lines?
explanations: Three is the number of input lines.
Six is not 2³.
Correct: A decoder with 3 inputs can select one of 2³=8 outputs.
Sixteen outputs require four input bits.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic.

questions.stem: A direct-mapped cache has 64 lines and a block size of 16 bytes. For a byte address, how many low-order bits are used for the block offset?
explanations: 2 bits select only 4 byte positions.
Correct: 16-byte block requires log₂16=4 offset bits.
6 bits would be the line-index bits for 64 lines.
10 is the combined offset and index width.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization.

questions.stem: If X and Y are independent random variables with finite variances, then:
explanations: Correct: Independence implies zero covariance, so the variance of the sum is the sum of variances.
Subtracting variances is not the formula for a sum.
The product variance is not generally the product of variances.
Independent variables have covariance zero, not necessarily one.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics.

questions.stem: Which statement about context-free languages is correct?
options: They are closed under intersection with every context-free language.
They are closed under intersection with regular languages.
explanations: CFLs are not closed under intersection with arbitrary CFLs.
Correct: Intersecting a CFL with a regular language always yields a CFL.
CFLs are not closed under complement in general.
Regular languages are a proper subset of CFLs.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation.

questions.stem: A symbol table in a compiler is primarily used to store:
options: Identifier attributes such as type, scope and storage information
explanations: Machine instructions are emitted in later code-generation stages.
Correct: The symbol table records identifier metadata needed by semantic analysis and code generation.
Comments are generally discarded or handled separately.
Network packets are unrelated to compilation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design.

questions.stem: A page fault occurs and the referenced page is not in memory. If a free frame exists, the OS generally:
options: Loads the page into the free frame and updates page tables
explanations: Replacement is unnecessary when a suitable free frame exists.
Correct: The page is fetched into the free frame and mappings/status are updated.
A page fault is normally handled transparently if valid and resources permit.
Virtual memory remains enabled.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems.

questions.stem: A schedule is conflict-serializable if its precedence graph is:
explanations: Completeness is not the criterion.
Correct: A schedule is conflict-serializable exactly when its precedence graph has no directed cycle.
Strong connectivity would imply cycles for multi-vertex graphs.
Bipartiteness is unrelated to serializability.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: DBMS.

questions.stem: A TCP sender has congestion window 12 MSS and receives three duplicate ACKs. Under classic Reno behaviour, it typically:
options: Immediately resets cwnd to 1 MSS and enters slow start
Enters fast retransmit/fast recovery and retransmits the missing segment
explanations: That is associated with a timeout response, not the classic three-duplicate-ACK response.
Correct: Three duplicate ACKs trigger fast retransmit and fast recovery in Reno.
Duplicate ACKs do not ordinarily close the connection.
The congestion window is not doubled.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks.

questions.stem: Which statement about a cookie marked HttpOnly is correct?
options: It cannot be sent over HTTPS.
It is not accessible through ordinary client-side JavaScript APIs.
It is automatically encrypted at rest in the browser.
It prevents all cross-site request forgery.
explanations: HttpOnly does not determine whether HTTPS is used; Secure is a separate attribute.
Correct: HttpOnly restricts access through APIs such as document.cookie.
HttpOnly does not itself guarantee encryption at rest.
HttpOnly alone does not prevent CSRF.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies.

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: Which statement about Java interfaces is correct in modern Java?
options: An interface can contain only abstract methods.
An interface can declare default and static methods with bodies.
An interface can be instantiated directly.
An interface field can be a mutable instance variable.
explanations: Modern Java interfaces may also contain default, static and private methods.
Correct: Default and static methods may have implementations.
Interfaces cannot be directly instantiated.
Interface fields are implicitly public static final constants.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOP and Java.

questions.stem: In black-box testing, test cases are primarily derived from:
options: External specifications, inputs and expected outputs
explanations: Internal paths are central to white-box testing.

questions.stem: Statements: All water meters are devices. No device is an animal. Which conclusion necessarily follows?

questions.stem: A Poisson process has an average of two events per interval. What is the probability of observing zero events in one such interval?
explanations: Correct — for λ=2, P(X=0)=e⁻²(2⁰/0!)=e⁻².
Incorrect — e⁻¹ corresponds to λ=1, not the stated mean.

questions.stem: A random variable X has variance 5. What is Var(3X−4)?
explanations: Incorrect — multiplication by 3 changes variance by the square of 3.
Incorrect — variance is not multiplied by the absolute scale factor alone.

Correct — Var(aX+b)=a²Var(X), so Var(3X−4)=9×5=45.

questions.stem: For the upper-triangular matrix [[2, 5], [0, 3]], what are its eigenvalues?

Correct — the characteristic polynomial of a triangular matrix is determined by its diagonal entries, so its eigenvalues are 2 and 3.
Incorrect — the diagonal entries are positive and the eigenvalues are not their negatives.
Incorrect — the sum and product are 5 and 6, but the eigenvalues themselves are 2 and 3.

questions.stem: On the integers, define a relation aRb when 4 divides (a−b). Which set is the equivalence class of 1?
explanations: Incorrect — integers divisible by 4 form the equivalence class of 0.

Correct — the class contains exactly integers of the form 1+4k for integer k.
Incorrect — this omits negative representatives and includes numbers not congruent to 1 modulo 4.

questions.stem: If A and B are square matrices of the same order with det(A)=3 and det(B)=−2, what is det(AB)?
explanations: Correct — det(AB)=det(A)det(B)=3×(−2)=−6.
Incorrect — −1 is not the product of the given determinants.
Incorrect — the product is negative six, not one.
Incorrect — the sign is negative because det(B) is negative.

questions.stem: A finite undirected graph is connected and has at least one edge. Which condition is necessary and sufficient for it to contain an Euler circuit?

The graph must be a tree

Incorrect — a tree is not generally Eulerian.

questions.stem: Let T(0)=0 and T(n)=2T(n−1)+1 for n≥1. What is the closed form of T(n)?

Every month contains at least one birthday
Exactly one month contains two birthdays
At least two months are empty
explanations: Correct — placing 13 people into 12 month categories forces at least one category to contain two or more people.

questions.stem: A four-bit odd-parity generator must output 1 exactly when the four data bits contain an odd number of 1s. Which gate operation combines the four bits to produce that parity bit?
explanations: Incorrect — AND is 1 only when all four bits are 1, not whenever their count is odd.
Incorrect — OR is 1 for any nonzero input and does not distinguish odd from even parity.
Correct — cascading XOR gates produce 1 for an odd number of input 1s and 0 for an even number.
Incorrect — XNOR gives the complement of the odd-parity XOR result.

questions.stem: For a positive-edge-triggered D flip-flop, what value is transferred to Q at the active clock edge?

The XOR of D and the previous Q
The value of the clock signal
explanations: Incorrect — complementing D describes neither the normal D flip-flop characteristic nor its next-state rule.
Correct — at the active edge, the flip-flop samples D and stores that value as its next Q state.
Incorrect — the D flip-flop does not combine D and the previous Q using XOR.
Incorrect — the clock controls when sampling occurs; it is not the data input.

questions.stem: What is the 4-bit Gray-code equivalent of the binary number 1011?
explanations: Incorrect — binary and Gray representations are not identical except for special patterns.
Incorrect — XORing adjacent binary bits does not produce 1101 for 1011.
Correct — keep the most significant bit, then XOR adjacent binary bits to obtain 1110.
Incorrect — 1001 results from an incorrect adjacent-bit conversion.

questions.stem: An ideal pipeline has six stages and executes five instructions with no stalls. How many clock cycles are required from the first instruction entering the pipeline until the fifth instruction completes?
explanations: Incorrect — five cycles would not allow the six-stage latency to be completed.
Incorrect — six cycles completes only the first instruction, not all five.
Correct — an ideal k-stage pipeline needs k+n−1 cycles: 6+5−1=10.
Incorrect — 30 cycles is the non-pipelined total if each of five instructions takes six serial stage cycles.

questions.stem: During a block transfer using DMA, which statement is most accurate?
options: The CPU executes a separate load/store instruction for every transferred byte
The DMA controller transfers data between an I/O device and memory, typically interrupting the CPU on completion
The cache controller performs all disk scheduling
The I/O device writes directly into CPU registers without a bus
explanations: Incorrect — DMA avoids CPU handling of every byte or word in the block.
Correct — the DMA controller manages the block transfer over the system bus and can notify the CPU when it finishes.
Incorrect — cache control and disk scheduling are separate functions.
Incorrect — DMA transfers involve memory and I/O interfaces, not direct writing into CPU registers.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design; DMA and I/O interfaces.

questions.stem: In low-order memory interleaving across multiple equal-sized banks, how are consecutive memory addresses typically distributed?
options: Consecutive addresses are placed in successive banks in round-robin order
All consecutive addresses are placed in bank zero
Every address is replicated in every bank
Addresses are assigned only by the CPU opcode
explanations: Correct — low-order interleaving uses low-order address bits to select banks, distributing consecutive words among successive banks.
Incorrect — placing all consecutive addresses in one bank would not provide interleaving.
Incorrect — interleaving distributes addresses; it does not replicate every word.
Incorrect — memory-bank selection is based on address bits, not the instruction opcode.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design; memory interleaving.

questions.stem: In C, a function receives an ordinary integer parameter by value. If the function assigns a new value to that parameter, what happens to the caller's original integer variable?
options: It is unchanged unless the function receives and uses its address through a pointer
explanations: Incorrect — ordinary scalar arguments are copied into the function parameter; assignment does not directly modify the caller's object.
Correct — passing a pointer to the caller's object and dereferencing it is the usual way to modify that object from the function.
Incorrect — parameter passing does not change an object's storage duration or scope to global.
Incorrect — assigning to a by-value parameter is well-defined and does not itself cause undefined behaviour.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: ISO C standard N1570; function-call argument semantics.

questions.stem: In a max-heap represented as a binary tree, which ordering condition must hold for every parent with children?
options: The parent key is no greater than either child key
The parent key is at least as large as each child key
Every node has exactly two children
The left subtree must contain only even keys
explanations: Incorrect — that is the min-heap ordering condition.
Correct — a max-heap requires each parent key to be greater than or equal to its children.
Incorrect — a binary heap is complete but need not be a full binary tree.
Incorrect — heap order has no parity restriction on keys.
