questions.stem: Suppose X is normally distributed with mean 70 and standard deviation 10. Approximately what is P(X > 85)?
explanations: 0.9332 is approximately P(X<85), the complementary tail.
0.5 is the probability above the mean 70, not above 85.
0.1587 is the upper-tail probability beyond z=1, not z=1.5.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; source/basis: Standard normal distribution table; Devore, Probability and Statistics for Engineering and the Sciences

questions.stem: Which statement about two random variables with finite, non-zero variances and correlation coefficient zero is always valid?
options: They have no linear correlation, but they may still be dependent through a non-linear relationship
They must have identical probability distributions
explanations: Zero correlation does not in general imply independence; that implication needs additional conditions such as joint normality.
Correct. Zero correlation rules out linear association measured by covariance but does not rule out all dependence.
With positive standard deviations, zero correlation means covariance is zero, not positive.
Correlation zero places no requirement that the marginal distributions be identical.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; source/basis: Casella and Berger, Statistical Inference, correlation and independence

questions.stem: Which statement is the Cayley–Hamilton theorem for a square matrix A?
options: A is always equal to its transpose
Every eigenvalue of A is zero
A commutes with every matrix of the same order
A satisfies its own characteristic polynomial
explanations: The theorem does not assert that A is symmetric.
It does not force all eigenvalues to be zero.
Commutativity with every same-order matrix is false in general.
Correct. If p(λ)=det(λI−A) is the characteristic polynomial, then p(A)=0.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications; standard Cayley–Hamilton theorem

questions.subtopic: Generators of a finite cyclic group
questions.stem: How many generators does a cyclic group of order 18 have?
explanations: Correct. A cyclic group of order n has φ(n) generators; φ(18)=18(1−1/2)(1−1/3)=6.
9 elements are not generators of a cyclic group of order 18.
A cyclic group of order 18 has 18 elements but only six generators.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Gallian, Contemporary Abstract Algebra, cyclic groups and Euler's totient function

questions.stem: A real 3×3 matrix has three distinct real eigenvalues. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: It is diagonalizable over the real numbers
It must be the zero matrix
explanations: Correct. Eigenvectors associated with distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent, giving three independent eigenvectors and a diagonalization.
A zero matrix has only the eigenvalue zero, so it cannot have three distinct eigenvalues.
The determinant is the product of eigenvalues and need not be zero.
A matrix can have distinct real eigenvalues without being symmetric.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Lay, Linear Algebra and Its Applications, eigenvalues and diagonalization

questions.stem: For a group homomorphism φ:G→H, which property must the kernel ker(φ) have?
options: It is a normal subgroup of G
It must equal G in every homomorphism
It must contain every element of H
It must be a cyclic subgroup of prime order
explanations: Correct. The kernel is a subgroup and is normal because gkg⁻¹ maps to the identity for every g∈G and k∈ker(φ).
The kernel equals G only for the trivial homomorphism, not every homomorphism.
The kernel is a subset of G, not H.
A kernel need not be cyclic or have prime order.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; source/basis: Gallian, Contemporary Abstract Algebra, kernels and normal subgroups

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: How many different full parenthesizations are possible for a product of five ordered operands, where multiplication is binary and operand order cannot change?
explanations: Five is not the Catalan number for five ordered operands.
10 is not the count of full binary parenthesizations for five operands.
Correct. The count is the fourth Catalan number C₄ = (1/5)·binomial(8,4)=14.
42 is the fifth Catalan number, which corresponds to six ordered operands.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.stem: An eight-person team is available. How many three-person committees can be formed if two specified people are not allowed to serve together?
explanations: 44 subtracts too many committees containing the specified pair.
48 does not follow from the combination count.
Correct. There are C(8,3)=56 committees; C(6,1)=6 contain both specified people, so 56−6=50 are allowed.
56 counts every committee, including the six forbidden ones.

questions.subtopic: Leaf count from degree sequence of a tree
questions.stem: A finite tree has exactly two vertices of degree 3 and four vertices of degree 4; every other vertex is a leaf. How many leaves does the tree have?
explanations: Eight omits part of the degree excess contributed by the four degree-4 vertices.
Ten is still below the value required by the tree degree-sum identity.
Correct. For a tree, L=2+Σ(d−2)n_d=2+2(3−2)+4(4−2)=12 leaves.
Fourteen would require a larger total degree excess than the stated internal vertices provide.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic; source/basis: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, trees and degree-sum identities

questions.stem: How many non-negative integer solutions are there to x₁+x₂+x₃=10?
explanations: 45 is not the stars-and-bars count for three non-negative variables.
55 would correspond to a different total or number of variables.
Correct. Stars and bars gives C(10+3−1,3−1)=C(12,2)=66.
78 is not the binomial coefficient required by the formula.

questions.stem: For a cross-coupled NOR SR latch with active-high S and R inputs, which input combination is the forbidden or invalid condition?
explanations: Correct. With both NOR inputs asserted, both outputs are driven low, violating the complementary-state requirement; release can lead to an indeterminate state.
S=1, R=0 is the set condition for the conventional NOR latch.
S=0, R=1 is the reset condition.
S=0, R=0 is the hold condition for a NOR SR latch.

questions.stem: In a two-level sum-of-products circuit, two adjacent input combinations both produce output 1, but the corresponding minterms are covered by separate product terms with no common implicant. Which correction most directly removes the resulting static-1 hazard?
options: Delete one of the product terms
Add a redundant consensus/bridging product term that covers the adjacent transition
Replace every AND gate with an OR gate
explanations: Deleting a required product term may change the Boolean function rather than remove only the hazard.
Correct. A redundant consensus term provides overlapping coverage during the input transition and removes the static-1 hazard.
Inverting the output changes the function and does not solve the hazard as stated.
Replacing gate types indiscriminately changes the implemented logic.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; source/basis: Mano and Ciletti, Digital Design, hazards in combinational circuits

questions.subtopic: Implementing a Boolean function with a 4-to-1 multiplexer
questions.stem: A 4-to-1 multiplexer uses A and B as its select inputs to implement F(A,B,C)=Σm(1,2,6,7), with A as the most significant variable. Which data-input assignment (D0,D1,D2,D3) is correct for select codes AB=00,01,10,11?
explanations: Correct. For AB=00, F=C; for 01, F=C′; for 10, F=0; for 11, F=1.
This reverses the first two cofactors and the last two constants.
This assigns the cofactors to the wrong select combinations.
This also assigns the cofactors and constants to the wrong select codes.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; source/basis: Mano and Ciletti, Digital Design, Shannon expansion and multiplexer implementation

questions.stem: After adding two valid BCD digits, when must a BCD adder add 0110₂ to the four-bit sum?
options: Whenever the binary sum is odd
Only when the lower digit is zero
When the four-bit sum exceeds 1001₂ or a carry out occurs
Whenever the sum is less than 1001₂
explanations: Oddness of the sum is unrelated to BCD correction.
A zero lower digit is not the correction condition.
Correct. A binary sum above 9 is not a valid BCD digit; adding six corrects the digit, including the carry-out case.
A sum below or equal to 9 is already a valid BCD digit and needs no correction.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Digital Logic; source/basis: Mano and Ciletti, Digital Design, BCD addition

questions.stem: A cache uses a write-allocate policy. On a write miss, what normally happens?
options: The processor halts until the entire cache is invalidated
The missed block is brought into the cache and the write is then applied to that cached block
The write is discarded because the block is absent
Every cache line is copied to main memory
explanations: A write-allocate policy does not require halting or invalidating the entire cache.
Correct. Write-allocate fetches the missed block into the cache before or as the store is completed there.
The store is not discarded; the policy defines how the miss is handled.
Copying every cache line is unrelated to write allocation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design, cache write policies

questions.stem: In Tomasulo's dynamic scheduling algorithm, register renaming primarily eliminates which classes of data hazard?
options: Structural hazards in every functional unit
Both write-after-read (WAR) and write-after-write (WAW), while true RAW dependencies remain
All control hazards and branch mispredictions
explanations: RAW is a true data dependence and cannot be removed merely by renaming registers.
Register renaming is not a guarantee that all functional-unit structural conflicts disappear.
Correct. Renaming removes false name dependencies WAR and WAW; true RAW dependencies must still be respected.
Register renaming does not eliminate branch-control hazards.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture; source/basis: Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design, Tomasulo scheduling

questions.subtopic: Effective CPI with branch misprediction penalty
questions.stem: A processor has a base CPI of 1.0. Branches are 20% of instructions; 10% of branches are mispredicted, and each misprediction costs 3 extra cycles. Assuming no other stalls, what is the effective CPI?
explanations: 1.006 understates the product of branch frequency, misprediction rate and penalty.
1.03 omits one factor in the penalty calculation.
Correct. Extra CPI=0.20×0.10×3=0.06, so effective CPI=1.06.
1.60 treats every branch as a misprediction and overstates the penalty.

questions.stem: In C, which statement correctly describes `const int *p` compared with `int * const p`?
options: Both declarations make the pointed-to integer and the pointer itself unmodifiable
`const int *p` makes p itself unassignable, while `int * const p` makes the pointed-to integer unmodifiable
`const int *p` makes the pointed-to integer non-modifiable through p but allows p to be reassigned; `int * const p` fixes p but allows `*p` to be modified
Neither declaration has any effect on assignment
explanations: The declarations impose different constraints and do not both make both objects immutable.
The meanings are reversed in this option.
Correct. The first is a pointer to const int; the second is a const pointer to int.
Both declarations affect which assignments are permitted.

questions.subtopic: Deque implementation using a doubly linked list
questions.stem: A deque must support insertion and deletion at both the front and rear in O(1) time. Which linked representation supports these operations directly when both end pointers are maintained?
options: A singly linked list with only a head pointer
A doubly linked list with head and tail pointers
A binary search tree without parent links
A singly linked list with no tail pointer
explanations: With only a head pointer, deleting the rear node requires finding its predecessor.
Correct. A doubly linked list with head and tail pointers supports constant-time updates at both ends.
A binary search tree is not the direct representation for deque end operations.
Without a tail pointer, rear operations cannot generally be performed in constant time.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: Weiss, Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis, deques and linked-list representations

questions.stem: In Floyd's tortoise-and-hare algorithm for detecting a cycle in a singly linked list, how are the two pointers advanced during each iteration?
options: Both pointers advance by one node
The slow pointer advances by two nodes and the fast pointer by one
The slow pointer advances by one node and the fast pointer by two
The fast pointer moves to the last node on every iteration
explanations: If both move at the same speed, the method cannot force a catch-up within a cycle.
The speeds are reversed in this option.
Correct. The fast pointer gains one node per iteration relative to the slow pointer and eventually meets it if a cycle exists.
The fast pointer follows links; it does not jump directly to the last node.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; source/basis: Weiss, Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis, linked-list cycle detection

questions.stem: Counting sort is applied to n integer keys known to lie in the range 0 through k. What is its standard time complexity?
explanations: Counting sort is not comparison-based and does not require n log n comparisons.
Correct. Counting the key frequencies, forming cumulative counts and placing the n items takes Θ(n+k) time.
There is no k log n sorting step in the standard algorithm.
Quadratic time is not the standard counting-sort bound.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed., counting sort

questions.stem: Quickselect is used to find the kth smallest element in an unsorted array by partitioning around pivots. With randomised pivots, which complexity statement is correct?
options: Expected Θ(n) time, with Θ(n²) worst case
Expected Θ(n log n) time and Θ(n log n) worst case
Expected Θ(log n) time and Θ(n) worst case
explanations: Correct. Randomised Quickselect has expected linear time, although consistently poor pivots can produce quadratic worst-case time.
The expected bound is linear, not n log n, and the worst case can be quadratic.
The algorithm must inspect/partition a linear amount of data in the expected case.
Quadratic time is a worst-case possibility, not the cost in every case.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: CLRS, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed., randomized selection

questions.stem: In A* search for a shortest path, a heuristic h(n) is admissible when it:
options: Never overestimates the true minimum remaining cost to a goal
Always equals the exact remaining cost
Is greater than the true remaining cost at every non-goal node
Depends only on the number of edges already traversed
explanations: Correct. An admissible heuristic is optimistic: h(n)≤h*(n) for every node.
Equality is sufficient but not required; an admissible heuristic may underestimate.
Overestimation violates admissibility and can destroy the optimality guarantee.
The heuristic estimates remaining cost, not merely the path already travelled.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; source/basis: Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, A* search and admissible heuristics

questions.stem: Which statement is part of the pumping lemma for regular languages? For some pumping length p, every string s in L with |s|≥p can be written s=xyz such that:
options: |xy|≤p, |y|≥1, and xyᶦz belongs to L for every i≥0
|x|=|y|=|z| and xyz belongs to every language
y must be the final symbol of s
xyᶦz must be outside L for every i>1
explanations: Correct. These are the standard decomposition and pumping conditions for a regular language.
The lemma does not require equal-length pieces or membership in every language.
The pumped segment y occurs within the first p symbols, not necessarily at the end.
The pumping lemma requires all pumped strings to remain in L, not leave it.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., pumping lemma for regular languages

questions.stem: Rice's theorem states that which class of properties of Turing-machine-recognisable languages is undecidable?
options: Every syntactic property of a machine's state names
Only properties concerning the number of tape symbols
Every non-trivial semantic property of the language/function recognised or computed
explanations: Renaming states is a syntactic change and is not the subject of Rice's theorem.
The theorem is not restricted to tape-alphabet size.
Correct. Any non-trivial property depending on the language/function recognised by a Turing machine is undecidable in general.
Rice's theorem concerns Turing-computable behaviour, not only finite automata.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., Rice's theorem

questions.subtopic: Linear bounded automata and context-sensitive languages
questions.stem: Which computational model characterises the class of context-sensitive languages?
options: Unrestricted Turing machines with no space bound
explanations: Finite automata recognise regular languages.
Pushdown automata characterise context-free languages.
Unrestricted Turing machines recognise recursively enumerable languages.
Correct. Context-sensitive languages are exactly those recognised by linear bounded automata.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., context-sensitive languages

questions.stem: What is the defining capability of a universal Turing machine?
options: It accepts every language, including undecidable languages
It simulates the computation of an encoded Turing machine on an encoded input
It decides the halting problem for every machine-input pair
It uses no tape and therefore has constant memory
explanations: A universal machine does not decide every language.
Correct. Given an encoding of machine M and input w, it can simulate M on w step by step.
The halting problem remains undecidable; universality does not solve it.
A Turing machine uses an unbounded tape model; it is not a constant-memory device.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; source/basis: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., universal Turing machines

questions.stem: In compiler intermediate-code generation, what is the purpose of backpatching?
options: To allocate physical memory pages for source variables
To remove all loop statements from the source program
To fill in unresolved target addresses of jumps once the destination instruction locations are known
To convert every arithmetic expression into machine code immediately
explanations: Memory-page allocation is an operating-system responsibility, not backpatching.
Backpatching does not eliminate loops.
Correct. Forward jumps may be emitted before their target locations are known; backpatching fills those addresses later.
Intermediate code is not necessarily converted directly to final machine code at that point.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; source/basis: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools, backpatching

questions.stem: Which set most accurately describes typical contents of a procedure activation record (stack frame)?
options: Only the source file name and compiler version
Return address, saved registers/control information, parameters and local storage as required by the calling convention
Only global variables shared by every procedure
The complete executable image of the process
explanations: Source-file metadata is not the normal run-time contents of a stack frame.
Correct. An activation record typically stores return/control information, saved state, arguments and local variables, subject to the ABI.
Globals usually reside in static storage, not in each procedure's activation record.
The executable image is not copied into every call frame.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; source/basis: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools; standard run-time storage organisation

questions.stem: In a canonical LR(1) item written `[A → α·, a]`, what role does the terminal `a` play?
options: It is the first symbol already consumed by α
It is a nonterminal that must be pushed onto the parser stack
It specifies a lookahead terminal under which the completed production may be reduced
It is always the end-marker, regardless of the item
explanations: The symbols before the dot have been recognised; the lookahead is not the first consumed symbol.
The lookahead is a terminal, not a nonterminal to push as a grammar symbol.
Correct. The LR(1) lookahead restricts when the completed item may reduce, helping distinguish contexts.
The lookahead can be a terminal from the grammar; it is not always the end-marker.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; source/basis: Aho, Lam, Sethi and Ullman, Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools, LR(1) items

questions.stem: A process accesses a virtual page whose page-table entry is valid and whose page is already resident in RAM, but the translation is absent from the TLB. What normally occurs?
options: A TLB miss causes a translation lookup/page-table walk, but not necessarily a page fault
The operating system must terminate the process
The page must be fetched from disk in every case
The TLB miss proves that the virtual address is invalid
explanations: Correct. A TLB miss means the translation is not cached; the page table may still show a valid resident page.
A TLB miss is a normal event and does not by itself justify terminating the process.
A disk read is required only if the page is not resident and a page fault must be serviced.
The page can be valid even though its translation is absent from the TLB.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts, TLBs and demand paging

questions.stem: In the working-set model, WSSᵢ(Δ) for process i is best defined as:
options: The total number of pages ever allocated to the process
The number of distinct pages referenced by the process during the most recent window of Δ memory references/time units
The number of page faults since the process was created
The number of frames installed in the TLB
explanations: The working set is a recent locality measure, not every page ever allocated.
Correct. WSSᵢ(Δ) counts the distinct pages referenced within the chosen recent window Δ.
Page-fault count is a different statistic.
TLB entries are not the definition of a process's working set.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts, working-set model and thrashing

questions.stem: An operating system uses page-fault-frequency control with an upper and lower acceptable fault-rate threshold. If a process's page-fault rate rises above the upper threshold, the usual response is to:
options: Reduce the process's frame allocation immediately
Allocate additional frames to the process if available, or suspend/rebalance load if memory is exhausted
Disable the page table and use segmentation only
Increase the process's CPU time slice without changing memory allocation
explanations: Reducing frames would generally increase the page-fault rate further.
Correct. The high fault rate indicates insufficient resident frames; the OS may allocate more frames or reduce multiprogramming if none are available.
Page-fault-frequency control does not replace paging with segmentation.
A CPU time-slice change does not directly address the memory-pressure signal.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; source/basis: Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts, page-fault-frequency strategy

questions.stem: What does `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC)` produce in a SQL query?
options: A unique sequential row number within each department partition, ordered by descending salary
A count of all employees with the same salary
A ranking that always assigns equal numbers to tied salaries
explanations: The window function does not collapse rows into one aggregate row per department.
Correct. ROW_NUMBER assigns 1, 2, 3, ... separately within each department partition according to the specified ordering.
It does not count employees by salary.
Tied sort values still receive distinct row numbers; RANK or DENSE_RANK behave differently.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; source/basis: PostgreSQL documentation, window functions; Elmasri and Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems

questions.stem: What is the principal concurrency benefit of multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) in a transactional database?
options: It eliminates the need for transaction isolation
It stores only one physical version of every row
It forces every reader to acquire an exclusive lock on every row
It can let readers use a consistent snapshot while writers create newer row versions
explanations: MVCC does not eliminate isolation semantics; it is one way to implement them.
Multiple versions, rather than only one, are central to MVCC.
Readers generally do not need exclusive locks merely to read an MVCC snapshot.
Correct. Versioned reads can avoid many read-write blocking conflicts while preserving a transactionally consistent snapshot.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; source/basis: PostgreSQL documentation, MVCC introduction; Elmasri and Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems

questions.stem: A control-flow graph has E=10 edges, N=8 nodes and one connected component (P=1). What is its cyclomatic complexity?
explanations: E−N+2P is not 2 for these values.
The result is not 3 when the component term is included.
Correct. V(G)=E−N+2P=10−8+2=4.
5 would require one additional edge or a different graph count.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: McCabe, A Complexity Measure; Pressman and Maxim, Software Engineering, cyclomatic complexity

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of mutation testing in software quality assurance?
options: To measure execution speed under maximum load
To assess whether a test suite detects small, deliberately introduced faults in the program
To automatically convert source code from one language to another
To prove that the program contains no defects
explanations: Performance benchmarking is a different testing activity.
Correct. Mutants are small program changes; tests that detect them provide evidence about the fault-detection strength of the test suite.
Language translation is not the purpose of mutation testing.
No practical test technique proves the complete absence of all defects.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: ISTQB Foundation Level syllabus, test techniques; Pressman and Maxim, Software Engineering

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes software verification from software validation?
options: Verification checks conformance to specified requirements; validation checks whether the resulting system meets user needs
Verification is performed only after deployment; validation only before coding
Verification and validation are identical terms
Validation checks coding style, while verification checks market demand
explanations: Correct. Verification asks whether the product is being built according to specification; validation asks whether the right product is being built for users.
Both activities can occur throughout development; they are not restricted to those single phases.
They are related but distinct quality activities.
The definitions are reversed and do not capture the standard distinction.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Information Systems and Software Engineering; source/basis: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 software life-cycle processes; Pressman and Maxim, Software Engineering

questions.stem: What information does the TCP Selective Acknowledgment (SACK) option allow a receiver to report?
options: Only the total number of application bytes generated
Non-contiguous blocks of data that have been received successfully, so the sender can retransmit missing ranges more precisely
The IP address of every router on the path
explanations: SACK is not an application-byte-generation counter.
Correct. SACK reports received sequence-number blocks beyond the cumulative ACK, allowing more targeted retransmission.
DNS server configuration is unrelated to TCP acknowledgement options.
TCP SACK does not enumerate the IP routers traversed by a packet.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: RFC 2018, TCP Selective Acknowledgment Options: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2018

questions.stem: Which prefix is reserved for IPv6 link-local unicast addresses?
explanations: 2000::/3 is the global-unicast allocation range.
FC00::/7 is reserved for unique-local addresses.
Correct. FE80::/10 identifies link-local unicast addresses that are valid only on the local link.
FF00::/8 is the IPv6 multicast address range.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: RFC 4291, IP Version 6 Addressing Architecture: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291

questions.stem: An IPv6 router cannot forward a packet because it is larger than the next-link MTU. What is the normal IPv6 behaviour?
options: The router fragments the packet into smaller fragments
The router silently discards it and never informs the source
The router discards it and sends an ICMPv6 Packet Too Big message so the source can adjust packet size
The router converts the packet into an IPv4 datagram
explanations: IPv6 routers do not fragment packets in transit.
Silently discarding without the required feedback would prevent proper Path MTU Discovery.
Correct. The router sends ICMPv6 Packet Too Big; the source adapts the packet size or performs source fragmentation where appropriate.
IPv6 forwarding does not translate a packet into IPv4.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; source/basis: RFC 8201, Path MTU Discovery for IP version 6; RFC 4443, ICMPv6

questions.stem: In XML, what is the principal role of a namespace name such as `urn:example:inventory`?
options: It uniquely identifies an element/attribute vocabulary; it need not be a retrievable web page
It specifies the physical directory in which the XML file must be stored
It encrypts all elements using the named protocol
It determines the order in which XML elements are parsed
explanations: Correct. A namespace URI is an identifier used to distinguish names; XML processors do not have to retrieve it as a document.
A namespace name does not prescribe file-system storage.
Namespaces do not provide encryption.
Parsing order follows XML structure and grammar, not the namespace identifier.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: W3C, Namespaces in XML 1.0 Recommendation: https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-names/

questions.stem: In a JSP page, what is the type and purpose of the implicit object `out`?
options: A JDBC Connection used for database queries
A JspWriter used to write response content
A ServletContext used to access application-wide attributes
An HttpSession used to retain user-specific state
explanations: Database connections are not represented by the JSP `out` object.
Correct. `out` is the JspWriter associated with the response output stream.
The application-wide context is exposed through the `application` implicit object.
User-session state is exposed through `session`.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: Jakarta Server Pages specification, implicit objects; Oracle Java EE JSP tutorial

questions.stem: In PHP, which superglobal array normally contains form fields submitted in the body of an HTTP POST request using the standard form encoding?
explanations: $_GET contains query-string parameters.
$_SERVER contains server and request environment information.
Correct. $_POST contains form variables submitted using POST form encoding.
$_COOKIE contains cookie values sent by the browser.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: PHP Manual, Variables From External Sources: https://www.php.net/manual/en/reserved.variables.post.php

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the HTTP response directives `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Cache-Control: no-cache`?
options: Both require every response to be encrypted
no-store allows storage but requires revalidation; no-cache forbids storage
no-store forbids caches from storing the response; no-cache permits storage but requires revalidation before reuse
no-store applies only to cookies, while no-cache applies only to HTML
explanations: Neither directive is an encryption mechanism.
The meanings are reversed in this option.
Correct. `no-store` prohibits storage; `no-cache` allows storage but requires successful validation before reuse.
The directives apply to HTTP caching generally, not only cookies or HTML.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: RFC 9111, HTTP Caching, Cache-Control directives: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111

questions.subtopic: HTML async versus defer script loading
questions.stem: For a classic external script in HTML, which statement about the `defer` attribute is correct?
options: The script is downloaded in parallel and executed after document parsing, in document order
The script blocks parsing while it downloads and executes immediately
The script executes before the HTML parser reaches the script element
The script is executed only after the user clicks the page
explanations: Correct. Deferred classic scripts execute after parsing completes and preserve document order relative to other deferred classic scripts.
This describes a parser-blocking script without async/defer.
Execution before the parser reaches the element is not the defer behaviour.
The attribute does not make execution depend on a user click.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; source/basis: WHATWG HTML Living Standard, script processing model: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: In Java, a subclass declares a static method with the same signature as a static method in its superclass. How is the selected method normally determined?
options: By runtime overriding based on the object's dynamic class
By the reference/expression type at compile time; static methods are hidden, not overridden polymorphically
By the most recently loaded class file
By the value of the method's return object
explanations: Runtime overriding applies to instance methods, not static method dispatch.
Correct. Static method selection is based on the compile-time type of the qualifying reference or class name.
Class-loading order does not define static method selection.
A returned object's value does not determine which static method is invoked.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: Java Language Specification, §8.4.8.2, Hiding (by Class Methods)

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.subtopic: C++ virtual inheritance in diamond hierarchy
questions.stem: In a C++ diamond-shaped inheritance hierarchy, both intermediate classes inherit from the same base class. What is the purpose of declaring that base inheritance as `virtual`?
options: To make all base-class functions pure virtual
To prevent construction of any derived object
To force every method call to use static binding
To ensure the most-derived object contains one shared base-class subobject rather than duplicate base subobjects
explanations: Virtual inheritance does not make all base functions pure virtual.
It does not prohibit constructing the derived object.
It does not control static versus dynamic method binding.
Correct. Virtual base classes ensure a single shared base subobject in the most-derived object.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: C++ working draft, virtual base classes and multiple inheritance: https://eel.is/c++draft/class.mi

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: A Java class `Parent` declares only `Parent(int x)` and has no no-argument constructor. A subclass `Child` declares no constructor of its own. What happens when the source is compiled?
options: The compiler automatically passes zero to Parent(int)
The Child class is valid because constructors are inherited
Compilation fails because the generated default Child constructor attempts an unavailable no-argument super() call
The JVM chooses a Parent constructor at run time
explanations: Java does not invent an argument value for a superclass constructor.
Constructors are not inherited by subclasses.
Correct. The implicit default constructor for Child invokes super(); because Parent has no accessible no-argument constructor, compilation fails.
Constructor resolution is checked at compile time, not deferred to the JVM.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: Java Language Specification, §8.8 constructors and §8.8.7 constructor bodies

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.subtopic: C++ friend declaration and non-member access
questions.stem: A class `Box` contains the declaration `friend int compare(const Box&, const Box&);`. Which statement about `compare` is correct?
options: It becomes a virtual member function of Box
It remains a non-member function but may access Box's private and protected members
It can access only public members of Box
It is automatically called whenever two Box objects are compared
explanations: A friend declaration does not make the function a virtual member.
Correct. Friendship grants the named non-member access rights without making it a member of the class.
Access to private and protected members is the reason for the friend declaration.
The declaration grants access but does not define an automatic operator or invocation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: C++ working draft, friend declarations: https://eel.is/c++draft/class.friend

questions.topic: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA
questions.stem: A Java class implements two unrelated interfaces that provide the same default instance method signature. What must the class normally do to resolve the conflict?
options: Override the method and provide an implementation or explicitly select a suitable interface default
Do nothing; the JVM randomly chooses one default method
Declare both interfaces as abstract classes
explanations: Correct. The implementing class must resolve the inherited default-method conflict, commonly by overriding and optionally using `InterfaceName.super.method()`.
Java does not select conflicting defaults randomly.
Interfaces are not converted into abstract classes by this conflict.
Interfaces are part of the type declaration and cannot be deleted at runtime to resolve compilation.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: OOPS Concepts, Programming in C++ and JAVA; source/basis: Java Language Specification, §8.4.8 and §9.4.1, interface default methods

questions.subtopic: Gini impurity calculation for a binary decision-tree node
questions.stem: A decision-tree node contains 70% positive and 30% negative examples. Using Gini impurity G=1−Σpᵢ², what is the node's impurity?
explanations: 0.21 is the product of the two class proportions, not the stated Gini formula.
0.30 is the minority-class proportion, not the impurity.
0.70 is the majority-class proportion, not the impurity.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, decision-tree impurity measures

questions.stem: For a binary classifier, an ROC AUC of 0.90 is most accurately interpreted as:
options: The classifier is correct on exactly 90% of all records at every threshold
A randomly selected positive example is ranked above a randomly selected negative example with probability about 0.90
explanations: AUC is threshold-independent ranking performance, not accuracy at every threshold.
Correct. AUC has the probabilistic ranking interpretation for a randomly chosen positive-negative pair.
The false-positive rate varies with the selected threshold.
Precision depends on the threshold and class prevalence; it is not equal to AUC.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, ROC analysis

questions.stem: A k-nearest-neighbours classifier uses Euclidean distance. One numeric feature ranges from 0 to 1, while another ranges from 0 to 100,000. What is the main risk if the features are used without scaling?
options: The large-range feature can dominate the distance calculation and distort neighbour selection
The small-range feature is automatically multiplied by 100,000
The algorithm changes into a decision tree
explanations: Correct. Differences on a large numeric scale can dominate the sum of squared coordinate differences.
No automatic rescaling occurs in ordinary Euclidean distance.
Euclidean distance remains mathematically defined for these finite numeric features.
Feature scaling does not change k-NN into another classifier.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, data preprocessing and k-NN

questions.stem: In AdaBoost, how are training-example weights typically changed after a weak learner is fitted?
options: Misclassified examples receive increased relative weight so the next learner focuses more on them
All examples are permanently assigned equal weight after every round
Correctly classified examples always receive the largest weight
The algorithm discards every example classified incorrectly
explanations: Correct. AdaBoost increases the relative emphasis on misclassified examples when constructing the next weak learner.
The weights are updated, not reset permanently to equal values.
Correctly classified examples generally receive reduced relative emphasis compared with misclassified examples.
Misclassified examples are not simply discarded; their influence is increased.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, boosting and AdaBoost

questions.stem: Why do anomalies tend to receive shorter average path lengths in an Isolation Forest?
options: They are always assigned to the largest cluster
Random partitioning often isolates rare or unusual observations with fewer splits than common observations
The algorithm first computes the exact Euclidean distance to every other record
The algorithm trains a single maximum-margin hyperplane
explanations: Cluster size is not the principle used by Isolation Forest.
Correct. Unusual observations are easier to separate through random partitions and therefore tend to have shorter isolation paths.
Isolation Forest does not require exhaustive pairwise Euclidean-distance computation.
A maximum-margin hyperplane describes an SVM, not Isolation Forest.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Liu, Ting and Zhou, Isolation Forest; Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques

questions.stem: Which representation is central to the Eclat frequent-itemset mining algorithm?
options: A vertical layout storing, for each item, the transaction-ID set in which it occurs
A horizontal table of candidate itemsets generated only by breadth-first enumeration
A decision tree whose leaves are class labels
explanations: Correct. Eclat uses vertical transaction-ID lists (tidsets) and intersects them to calculate support of combined itemsets.
The horizontal candidate-generation description is closer to the classic Apriori approach.
A decision tree is a supervised classification model, not the Eclat representation.
A neural-network weight matrix is unrelated to frequent-itemset mining.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Han, Kamber and Pei, Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques, Eclat algorithm

questions.stem: In a support vector machine with a hard-margin linear separator, which training points determine the position of the maximum-margin decision boundary?
options: All training points equally, regardless of their distance from the boundary
Only the support vectors lying closest to the separating hyperplane
Only points classified correctly far from the boundary
Only points from the majority class
explanations: Distant non-support points do not individually determine the maximum-margin boundary once the margin constraints are satisfied.
Correct. The support vectors are the constraint-active points closest to the hyperplane and determine the maximum-margin separator.
Points far from the boundary generally do not define the margin.
The support vectors can come from both classes; majority-class membership is not the rule.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; source/basis: Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning; standard support-vector-machine maximum-margin formulation

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: According to ISRO's 28 October 2026 mission update, which launcher successfully placed the NVS-03 spacecraft into its intended orbit?
explanations: PSLV-C62 was associated with the separate EOS-N1 mission, not NVS-03.
Correct. ISRO reported that GSLV-F18 successfully placed NVS-03 in its intended orbit.
LVM3-M6 carried a different commercial payload in 2025.
SSLV-D3 was an earlier small-satellite launch vehicle mission.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs; source/basis: ISRO, GSLV-F18/NVS-03 Mission update, 28 Oct 2026; https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/Mission_GSLVF18.html

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: At the June 2026 Mahila Varotsavalu programme, how many buses owned by women's self-help groups were handed over to TGSRTC for operation?
explanations: 253 is not the number stated in the Telangana release.
403 is not the figure in the programme report.
Correct. The Telangana State Portal reported 553 SHG-owned buses being handed over to TGSRTC.
1,053 combines no figure stated for this handover.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: Government of Telangana, Mahila Varotsavalu–2026 press release, 9 Jun 2026; https://www.telangana.gov.in/news/press-releases/2026/06/honble-cm-sri-revanth-reddy-participated-in-mahila-varotsavalu-2026-flags-off-shg-women-owned-buses-at-parade-grounds-secunderabad/

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: ISRO reported completing a set of tests for the Gaganyaan programme in 2026. Which separation was specifically named in the announcement?
explanations: Correct. ISRO's announcement specifically described Crew Module–Service Module separation tests.
The announcement did not describe separation of a solid booster from a liquid core.
Gaganyaan is an Indian human-spaceflight programme, not a lunar-lander mission.
Parachute deployment and crew-escape testing are different test activities.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: ISRO, Crew Module-Service Module Separation Tests for Gaganyaan Programme, 16 Oct 2026; https://www.isro.gov.in/Crew_Module_Service_Module_Separation_Tests.html

questions.topic: Current affairs – Regional, National and International
questions.stem: The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 were notified by which Union ministry?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
explanations: The Home Ministry was not the notifying ministry for these rules.
Correct. The Gazette notification identifies the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
The Department of Telecommunications is not the issuing ministry named in the Gazette.
The Gazette identifies MeitY, not the Ministry of Law and Justice, as the notifying ministry.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Current affairs – Regional, National and International; source/basis: Gazette of India, MeitY notification G.S.R. 846(E), Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, 13 Nov 2025; https://egazette.gov.in/

questions.stem: Under the Statute of the International Court of Justice, how many judges constitute the Court, and what is the normal term of office?
explanations: The Statute does not provide for a 12-member Court with six-year terms.
Correct. The ICJ consists of 15 independent judges elected for nine-year terms.
The Court has neither 18 judges nor five-year terms.
The Court is not composed of 21 judges serving four-year terms.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations and Events; source/basis: Statute of the International Court of Justice, Articles 3 and 13; United Nations

questions.subtopic: UN Economic and Social Council composition
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the membership and normal term of the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)?
explanations: ECOSOC membership was expanded beyond 36 members.
47 is the membership of the Human Rights Council, not ECOSOC.
Correct. ECOSOC has 54 members elected by the General Assembly for three-year terms.
ECOSOC does not have 60 members or five-year terms.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations and Events; source/basis: UN Charter, Article 61; United Nations ECOSOC institutional profile

questions.stem: A country elected as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council normally serves for which period?
options: Two years, without immediate re-election for the next term
Three years, with one consecutive re-election
Five years, matching the permanent members
explanations: The normal elected term is not one year.
Correct. Non-permanent members serve two-year terms and are not immediately eligible for re-election at the end of their term.
The elected term is two years, not three.
Five-year tenure applies to no Security Council category; permanent members do not have fixed terms.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: International Relations and Events; source/basis: UN Charter, Article 23; United Nations Security Council membership rules

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.stem: In a drinking-water treatment system, what is the principal mechanism by which UV-C disinfection inactivates many microorganisms?
options: It removes dissolved calcium and magnesium ions
It damages microbial nucleic acids so that replication is impaired
It converts dissolved salts into insoluble precipitates
It raises water alkalinity to a lethal level
explanations: UV disinfection does not function as a hardness-removal process.
Correct. UV-C damages DNA or RNA, preventing effective replication and infection.
Precipitation of dissolved salts is a chemical softening or treatment process, not the UV mechanism.
UV treatment does not disinfect by increasing water alkalinity.
